fields.claim_quote: Note that LD $\;s_L$-code $X$ can contain  $\le L-1$ bad columns.
fields.explanation: Preserves all six original column supports, using Finset (Fin 6) and a harmless 1-based to 0-based row relabelling. Finset.biUnion is the Boolean disjunct union of supports, and coverage_iff_boolean proves equivalence to coordinatewise coverage by the corresponding Boolean characteristic columns. The source LD condition quantifies over every Finset of column names, requiring each four-element selection to cover at most one unselected column. Badness quantifies over every two-element Finset of other column names, so the source distinctness and floor(4/2)=2 arity are exact. The theorem proves all global source parameter restrictions, six distinct columns, LD validity, and badColumns={A,B,C} with cardinality three>1, then refutes the universal bound. All manual Boolean cardinality and pair enumeration has been replaced by Mathlib finite-set operations. The quoted claim is from the stored original-v1 source, Proposition 2, lines 533–542; the stable record identifier retains the flagged-v6 suffix, which is not a claim that the quotation was checked in version 6.
fields.flaw: Every LD s_L-code with s>L≥2 contains at most L−1 bad columns, where a bad column is covered by the disjunct sum of floor(s/L) other columns.
fields.problem: Title: Bounds on the rate of superimposed codes

0533 | \textbf{Proposition 2.}\quad
0534 | Let $s>L\ge2$, and $X$ be an arbitrary LD $\;s_L$-code of length $N$ and size~$t$.
0535 | A column (codeword) of  $X$  is called  \emph{bad} for $X$, if  $X$ contains
0536 | $\len s/L\rin$ other columns such that their disjunct sum covers the given column.
0537 | Otherwise, we   say that the column is \emph{good} and, obviously,  the set of all good
0538 | columns is a classical superimposed $\len s/L\rin$-code.
0539 | Note that LD $\;s_L$-code $X$ can contain  $\le L-1$ bad columns.
0540 | Actually, if there exists an $L$-collection of bad columns of $X$, then the given  $L$-collection
0541 | is covered by a disjunct sum of  $\;\le\, L\cdot\len s/L\rin\le s\;$ columns of $X$. This
0542 | contradicts to the definition of LD $\;s_L$-code.
0543 | In other words, any  $\;s_L$-code of size~$t$  and length~$N$ contains at least  $\; t-(L-1)\;$ codewords
0544 | constituting a superimposed  $\len s/L\rin$-code of  length~$N$. Therefore, the maximal size
0545 |    $t_{ld}(N,s,L)$ and the rate $R_L(s)$ satisfy inequalities
0546 | \beq{lb-triv2}
0547 | t_{ld}(N,s,L)\,\le\,t_{ld}\left(N,\len s/L\rin,1\right)+L-1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
0548 | R_L(s)\,\le\,R\left(\len s/L\rin,1\right),
0549 | \quad L\le s.
0550 | \eeq

fields.witness: Take s=4, L=2, so floor(s/L)=2. Represent six binary columns by supports: A={1,2}, B={1,3}, C={2,3}, D={4}, E={5}, F={6}. Then A⊆B∪C, B⊆A∪C, and C⊆A∪B. Thus A,B,C are three bad columns, exceeding L−1=1. The six columns also satisfy the LD condition. Any four-column selection leaves two columns outside. If an omitted column is D, E or F, its private coordinate is absent from the selected columns, so that column is not covered. If both omitted columns lie among A,B,C, only one of that triple is selected, and its support covers neither omitted column. Thus at most one outside column is covered by any four-column selection, as required for L=2.
